Title: MOF warns against fake Threads account using Treasury sec-gen's identity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public have been advised to beware of a fake Threads account using the name and photograph of Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
In a Facebook post today, the Finance Ministry (MoF) urged the public not to share personal information or engage with the account.
It also cautioned against following, trusting or sharing content from the fake account to prevent confusion and identity misuse.
"Ensure that all information received is verified through the Finance Ministry's official communication channels," the post said.
The post also included a screenshot of the fake Threads account bearing Johan's name and photograph.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police investigate viral claims of extortion, bribery at Penang roadblock
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police are investigating a viral social media post alleging that traffic policemen had committed extortion and accepted bribes during a roadblock.
Northeast police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said they detected the post today after it drew widespread public attention.
He confirmed that a police report had been lodged.
"Police are investigating the incident depicted in the viral post involving the traffic personnel under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998," he said in a statement.
Rozak said the investigation would also cover compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and disciplinary aspects involving the personnel concerned.

Title: Fadhlina: Character building must begin at preschool level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Values education and character building should begin at preschool age to nurture respect and empathy in children.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said quality education was not merely about teaching children to read, write and count, but also about shaping them into individuals with good values and strong character.
"This effort certainly requires the support of parents, teachers and the community at large. What is taught in school must also be nurtured at home, as children learn not only from what we tell them but also from what they observe in their daily lives," she said in a Facebook post today.
Fadhlina also expressed her appreciation for the concern and views expressed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over increasingly worrying social issues involving the young generation.
"The concern by His Royal Highness serves as a reminder that efforts to shape a child's character cannot wait until they reach their teenage years," she said.
On Nov 18, Tuanku Muhriz voiced concern over the rise in social problems among youths, prompting the introduction of the Modul Aulad Sejahtera (Child Well-being Module), an early intervention initiative aimed at shaping character, instilling noble values and strengthening children's identity from the preschool level.
His Royal Highness said the module was developed in response to worrying social trends, including drug abuse, illegal street racing and other negative behaviours that threaten the future of the young generation.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said 8,365 preschool pupils under the Education Ministry (MOE) in Negri Sembilan would benefit from the Modul Aulad Sejahtera, which emphasises the development of good conduct (adab), noble values, emotional well-being and social skills.
She expressed hope that the initiative, introduced in Negri Sembilan, could serve as a model for nurturing a knowledgeable generation with strong cultural values.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rough waters no reason to sink the ship, Abang Johari tells GPS members
Article:
KUCHING:KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) component parties must remain united and not allow differences of opinion to sink the coalition's ship as it navigates the rough waters ahead of the 13th Sarawak state election, says its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The Sarawak Premier said differences of opinion were inevitable during an election, but the coalition's component parties must ensure that such differences did not derail their shared goals.
He said the entire election machinery must work together to keep the GPS vessel on course, guided by a spirit of camaraderie.
"During an election, all sorts of things happen. Which sea is without rough waters? There are bound to be some waves, but do not sink the ship. Let the ship, with its captain and crew, sail toward a glorious destination.
"The engines must be in good working order, and the technicians tending to them must be able to read the compass. If the compass isn't set correctly, you'll end up somewhere else.
"You need people who know how to read the 'GPS compass'. We have a compass, a 'GPS' compass crafted by Sarawakians, so let us move forward," he said during the launch of the GPS election machinery at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK).
Abang Johari, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) president, said the spirit of camaraderie, rooted in firm mutual trust, must be upheld to ensure political stability and the state's development.
Earlier, Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) president Datuk Seri
Tiong King Sing
said his party intended to defend all eight state seats it currently held in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Tiong expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party's election machinery, coupled with the commitment of its leadership and members, would ensure that all eight seats remained with PDP under the GPS coalition.
GPS comprises PBB, Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.
The
Election Commission
has set Nov 28 as nomination day, Dec 8 for early voting and Dec 12 as polling day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak polls: PDP to defend eight seats under GPS banner
Article:
KUCHING: The Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) aims to defend all eight state legislative assembly seats currently held by the party in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Party president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party machinery, combined with the commitment of the entire PDP leadership and its members, would ensure that all eight seats remain under the party's fold within the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) coalition.
"As the party president, I wish to emphasise that we intend to retain all eight seats currently held by the PDP. I have full confidence in the wisdom and leadership of Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to continue safeguarding harmony within GPS," he said.
He made these remarks while speaking at the launch of the Gabungan Parti Sarawak election machinery for the 13th Sarawak state election.
Meanwhile, Tiong clarified that he has not yet submitted the PDP's list of candidates, despite claims circulating that the list had already been handed over to the GPS leadership.
He said his party's list of candidates would be submitted to Abang Johari who also serves as the chairman of GPS no later than this coming Monday and will take into account the views of the coalition's leadership regarding candidate selection criteria, including factors such as age.
Five of the eight seats currently held by PDP, namely, Tasik Biru, Meluan, Krian, Marudi, and Dudong were won by the party during the 12th Sarawak state election while the remaining seats of Bawang Assan, Engkilili, and Ba'kelalan were acquired following the dissolution of Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) and the subsequent absorption of its members into the PDP as a bloc.
Abang Johari was reported as saying that the full list of the coalition's 82 candidates for the Sarawak state election will be announced on Nov 25.
The Election Commission (EC) has set the polling day for the 13th Sarawak state election for Dec 12, with nomination day scheduled for November 28 and early voting for Dec 8.

Title: GST should start at 3pct to ease cost of living, says consumer group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The next government should consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at an initial rate of three per cent to ease the cost of living, says the Kedah Consumers Association (CAKE).
Its president, Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff, said the proposed rate would be more reasonable than the previous six per cent, given that prices of essential goods were already high compared with income levels.
He said the rising cost of living had put pressure on consumers and businesses, as declining purchasing power led to slower sales.
"If the GST can help ease the burden on the people, it should be introduced at a lower rate of three per cent initially.
"At the same time, we hope full exemptions will be granted for essential goods and purchases made by those in the bottom 40 per cent income group (B40) to ease their financial burden," he said.
He was commenting on a statement by Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who pledged to reintroduce the GST if the coalition returned to power after the 16th general election (GE16).
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister,
described the GST
as a fairer and more targeted taxation system than the Sales and Service Tax (SST) currently in place.
He said more than 170 countries had implemented the GST and that Malaysia should reinstate it to avoid falling behind other nations.
On the differences between the GST and SST, Mohamad Yusrizal said the current SST system resulted in overlapping or multiple layers of taxation along the supply chain.
He said the eight per cent tax imposed at different stages, from manufacturers to wholesalers and retailers, contributed to a gradual increase in the final prices of goods.
"In contrast, the GST allows manufacturers and wholesalers to claim input tax credits, making the calculation process more transparent and fair.
"However, confusion arose previously due to a lack of clear explanations to consumers.
"The detailed breakdown of taxes on purchase receipts also made people feel more burdened compared with the SST, where taxes are incorporated into selling prices," he said.
Meanwhile, Yusrizal said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry should take more proactive measures to prevent unjustified price increases.
He said the ministry already had the necessary legal provisions under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 to curb profiteering and protect consumer rights.
"The ministry should fully utilise the existing legislation to prevent profiteering and safeguard consumers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shoes tax break: Cultivating a culture of well-being
Article:
LETTER:
At first glance, the act of including sports shoes in the tax relief list under Budget 2027 might seem like a rather small, even amusing, announcement.
We should look beyond the shoes themselves and consider what this measure represents. Malaysia is facing a growing public health challenge.
The Ministry of Health's National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024: Nutrition found that 30.5 per cent of Malaysian adults were overweight, 23.1 per cent were obese and more than half, or 52.1 per cent, also had abdominal obesity.
Being overweight can increase the risk of health problems such as diabetes and heart disease, which may require long-term treatment and add to the demands on our healthcare system.
These findings highlight the scale of the challenge facing the country, with implications for families, workplaces, and public resources.
Earlier findings from NHMS 2023 showed that 29.9 per cent of adults were physically inactive, underlining the importance of creating more opportunities for Malaysians to lead active lives.
Obesity is rarely the result of one decision or one bad habit.
It develops through a combination of factors, including diet, physical activity, working patterns, the environment, and access to opportunities for healthier living.
For Malaysians balancing work, family commitments and the rising cost of living, finding time for exercise can easily take a back seat.
This is where the seemingly ordinary pair of sports shoes becomes relevant.
For someone who already runs regularly, the tax relief may simply be a welcome saving on a purchase they would have made anyway.
But for someone who has been thinking about taking up walking or starting a simple exercise routine, it could provide a small push in the right direction.
It may not be the deciding factor, but it can help make the first step feel a little more achievable.
For beginners, especially those who are overweight or have not exercised for years, comfort and appropriate support may influence whether they continue an activity or abandon it after a few uncomfortable attempts.
Of course, we should be clear about what the Budget 2027 measure offers. The inclusion of sports shoes under the existing sports-related tax relief does not mean every Malaysian will receive free shoes or a cash payment.
Under Budget 2027, eligible taxpayers can claim tax relief on sports shoes, subject to a limit of RM300 within the existing overall sports-related tax relief limit of RM1,000.
The challenge is to ensure that the tax relief forms part of a broader effort rather than remaining a standalone measure.
Encouraging people to buy sports shoes is only useful if it leads them to be physically active.
More parks and recreational spaces are needed, while walking paths should be properly maintained and extended to more urban areas.
These improvements would make walking more accessible and encourage people to choose it over driving whenever practical.
Workplaces can also play a role by introducing wellness programmes, organising group walks or exercise sessions, and allowing employees reasonable breaks to move throughout the working day.
We must also move away from the idea that exercise is reserved for people who are already fit.
A healthier lifestyle does not have to begin with a marathon, an expensive gym membership, or a demanding workout programme.
It can begin with a ten-minute walk after dinner, taking the stairs when practical, or walking to a nearby shop instead of driving.
These may appear insignificant individually, but they can help establish habits that become part of everyday life.
The sports shoe tax relief is therefore best understood as a modest incentive, not a cure.
Its success should not be measured by how many pairs of shoes Malaysians purchase, but by whether it contributes to a wider culture that values movement, prevention, and personal well-being.
A government that recognises the importance of exercise in its fiscal policies is acknowledging that health deserves attention beyond hospitals and clinics.
NUR FARAH IDAYU SAADON
Training consultant
National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DOSM to conduct household income, expenditure and basic amenities survey next year
Article:
IPOH: The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) will conduct the 6th Household Income, Expenditure and Basic Amenities Survey (HIES/BA) 2027 from Jan 1 to Dec 31 next year.
In a statement, DOSM said the survey aims to collect data on household income, expenditure, and basic amenities to produce official statistics regarding expenditure patterns, poverty rates, cost of living, and income inequality.
"The statistics produced serve as a basis for planning and policy formulation by stakeholders toward improving the well-being of the people," according to the statement.
In the same statement, DOSM said it provides a data catalog and visualisations to facilitate users in analysing various data through OpenDOSM NextGen, which can be accessed via the portal https://open.dosm.gov.my.
Meanwhile, DOSM implemented six community development projects worth RM500,000 in Kampung Menderang, Sungkai, through the Kampung Angkat Madani 2026 Programme.
The initiative is a strategic collaboration between the government and the local community to empower rural development inclusively and sustainably, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspirations.
"All completed projects include the construction of basic village facilities and infrastructure, the installation of signboards, and the installation of solar lights around the area.
"In addition, the development initiative also includes upgrading works for mosque, surau, and sports court facilities," the statement said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood situation improves in Selangor, Perak as evacuee numbers drop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Flood situations in Selangor and Perak continued to improve, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres declining to 2,151 people from 615 families this afternoon, compared with 2,315 people from 689 families this morning.
In
SELANGOR
, the number dropped to 1,727 people from 484 families, compared with 1,884 people from 532 families recorded this morning.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, the evacuees were housed at several relief centres, including SK Dato' Maharaja Lela (397), SK Parit Mahang (360), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (180), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (135), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120) and SK Rantau Panjang (four).
Other centres were SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (223 evacuees), SK Jaya Setia (73), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (65), Seri Harmoni Community Hall (36), SK Batu Arang (25), Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (16) and SRA Pasangan (93).
In
PERAK
, the number of evacuees at five relief centres in four districts also dropped to 424 people from 131 families this afternoon, compared with 479 people from 157 families this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the SK Tanjung Belanja relief centre in Perak Tengah was closed at 2 pm after all 53 evacuees from 25 families were allowed to return home after floodwaters receded.
Meanwhile, SRA Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung recorded 129 evacuees from 38 families, while the Teluk Intan Municipal Council Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak continued to house 97 people from 31 families.
In Kerian, the number of evacuees remained unchanged at 176 people from 55 families, including 12 landslide victims from three families, who were sheltering at SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman.
The number of flood evacuees in Larut, Matang and Selama also remained unchanged at 10 people from four families, housed at SK Batu Hampar.

Title: Seven body bags recovered, 50 missing after Indonesian factory fire
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police recovered seven body bags and rescuers were searching for about 50 workers who were missing on Sunday after a fire tore through a factory in western Java, as firefighters tackled hotspots over a day after the blaze broke out.
One body bag might contain body parts from several people, police said.
Authorities said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable via visual inspection, prompting efforts to collect DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers.
"Seven body bags have been recovered," said Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official.
"We have concluded that the victims of this fire cannot be identified through visual inspection."
She attributed this to the intensity of the fire, which had not been completely extinguished, adding that the identification process could take two to three weeks.
To aid identification efforts, authorities are collecting DNA samples from the relatives of missing workers and gathering personal belongings from their homes or dormitories to help establish the victims' identities.
The factory owner said at a news conference that around 300 people were present for the day's shift.
"The figure of 50 refers to those whom we have not yet been able to account for," he said.
The fire broke out on Saturday evening at a candy factory in Cikande, in the Serang regency. Authorities said the cause of the fire was being investigated.
Search teams were combing sections of the damaged building where victims were believed to be trapped, while parts of the building remained at risk of collapse, an official said.
The factory is part of Indonesia's United Family Food company, founded in 1981, according to its website.
It produces consumer goods across Indonesia, employs about 5,000 people and operates from its national headquarters and four international offices, serving a market of more than 250 million consumers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Death toll from spurious liquor in India's Manipur rises to 16
Article:
NEW DELHI: The death toll from spurious liquor consumption in India's northeastern state of Manipur has risen to 16, while around 600 people are undergoing treatment in different hospitals, officials said Saturday, reported Xinhua.
The incident took place in the Chakpikarong area of Chandel district, about 75 km south of Imphal, the capital city of Manipur.
"The death toll in the spurious liquor incident has risen to 16," a local government official said.
According to the state-run broadcaster All India Radio (AIR), around 600 people have been admitted to various government and private hospitals.
A senior local government official in Manipur, Hungyo Worshang, told the media that teams from the district administration, police, excise and health departments have visited the affected areas and hospitals to assess the situation and provide necessary assistance.
Police have arrested six people in connection with the incident.
The local government of Manipur has constituted a high-level inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify possible lapses and recommend necessary action.
Officials said the committee has been asked to submit its report within one month.
"Samples of the suspected liquor have been sent for forensic examination to identify the presence of toxic substances," the official said.
Manipur health department has issued a public health advisory in view of the suspected spurious liquor-related deaths and illnesses.
The health department has directed all government and private healthcare facilities to remain alert and ensure prompt treatment, referral and reporting of suspected cases.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lahore tops the list of most polluted cities in the world
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Hazardous smog turned Pakistan's second-largest city into the most polluted metropolis on the planet on Sunday, leaving authorities helpless to curb pollution, reported German news agency dpa.
The air quality in Lahore had a pollutant concentration reading of 289, making it the most-polluted city in the world, according to IQAir, a global environmental think tank.
The eastern city bordering India consistently ranked as the world's most polluted major city in the past few weeks since thick and hazardous smog engulfed parts of the central Punjab province.
Motorways connecting major cities were closed for traffic due to poor visibility at various points by authorities in addition to anti-smog measures that include fines on smoke-emitting vehicles.
Pakistani authorities blame industrial emissions, smoke from brick kilns and vehicles, the burning of crop residue and general waste for being behind the air pollution and smog in Lahore.
Pakistan is responsible for less than one per cent of global carbon emissions but is among the top 10 most climate-vulnerable nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chow rejects Guan Eng's 'unethical' Penang-Perak water deal claims
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has rebuked Bagan member of parliament Lim Guan Eng for repeatedly alleging unethical conduct in the Perak-Penang bulk water deal.
Chow, who chairs PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) and Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP), said it was regrettable that Lim continued to repeat the allegations despite repeated explanations about the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA).
In a statement, Chow questioned why securing 40 years of water supply for residents, industries, investors and future generations could be considered unethical.
He said the agreement had received approval from all PBAPP board members and secured 98 per cent shareholder support at PBAHB's extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Nov 12.
Addressing concerns over the board's decision, Chow said the views and professionalism of five PBAHB independent directors had been recorded and respected during the meeting, which passed the agreement by a majority vote of seven to five.
"Their objections were solely focused on specific payment terms, which have already been addressed through clauses in the agreement," he said.
Lim had recently accused Chow of acting
unethically
by dismissing concerns over the state's RM8.4 billion water deal with Perak.
He said Chow had disrespected the financial judgement and professionalism of five independent directors of PBAHB who objected to the agreement's terms.
Chow also dismissed Lim's allegation that PBAPP would be forced to pay RM210 million annually for 40 years without receiving a single drop of water, describing the portrayal as misleading and unethical.
He said PBAPP was not required to make any payment to Perak before water supply implementation began, and any disbursement remained subject to approval by the National Water Services Commission.
Under the arrangement, Penang would gain access to substantial water infrastructure capacity without bearing the full construction costs and early-stage development risks.
Chow added that PBAPP held contractual rights to take action, including invoking termination mechanisms, if unrectified breaches occurred.
"This means Penang is not locked into paying until 2072 as claimed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi allocates RM50k for mass communication students
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has announced a RM50,000 contribution to a coalition of mass communication student clubs to encourage student development programmes.
The contribution is aimed at strengthening the coalition and helping students face future challenges, particularly the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on journalism and mass communication, he said.
Fahmi also proposed expanding the coalition to all public universities before bringing private universities offering mass communication courses on board.
"I welcome the formation of a coalition of student clubs from mass communication courses or faculties. I understand that five universities are represented today.
"To encourage them to plan programmes in the future, I am announcing a contribution of RM50,000 to the coalition.
"I have also asked for it to be expanded to all public universities and subsequently to private universities with mass communication faculties or courses," he said.
He was speaking after officiating the Communication and Media Student National Convention, organised by Universiti Teknologi MARA's Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, here today.
Also present was UiTM Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic and International) Professor Dr Yamin Yasin, who is performing the functions of the vice-chancellor.
Fahmi said students had frequently raised concerns about their career prospects, particularly the impact of AI on journalism, during his engagements at universities.
He said he wanted to increase engagement with students to hear their concerns and explain the government's efforts to protect journalists' jobs and the future of journalism and mass communication in the age of AI.
"I see the need for more engagement with university students, not only to listen to their concerns but also to explain the government's efforts, particularly to protect journalists' jobs and the future of journalism and mass communication with the presence of AI," he said.
Fahmi also acknowledged the contributions of strategic partners, including Bank Muamalat and Tenaga Nasional Berhad, to student development programmes.
He hoped partnerships, particularly with government-linked companies and corporate bodies, would help expand such programmes and bring them closer to university students.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Inaccurate descriptions of missing people's journeys could affect insurance claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Inaccurate descriptions of the journeys of 54 Malaysians still missing after Nepal-Tibet floods could complicate their families' insurance claims, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) said.
MASFIH coordinator and spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said describing the missing Malaysians as participants in climbing activities and expeditions did not reflect the purpose of their journeys and could complicate claims.
He said insurance policies could contain specific terms, conditions and exclusions for high-risk activities such as climbing and mountaineering.
"We do not want families, who have already endured prolonged uncertainty over their loved ones, to face further questions and difficulties because of inaccurate descriptions of their journeys," he said in a statement.
Manivannan said 42 of the missing Malaysians were on a religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, while the remaining 12 were tourists travelling by jeep towards Tibet to enjoy Nepal's scenery.
He said neither group was taking part in climbing or mountaineering expeditions.
"It is important to distinguish between religious pilgrimages, ordinary tourism and climbing activities. Visiting mountainous areas or enjoying natural landscapes does not mean someone is taking part in hiking, mountaineering or climbing expeditions," he said.
Manivannan said MASFIH's request for a face-to-face meeting with the Foreign Ministry, first made on Sept 27, was still awaiting a date.
The meeting was intended to clarify the process for declaring a person presumed dead in Nepal, its recognition and legal implications in Malaysia, the required documents and the protection of families' rights if someone declared presumed dead was later found alive.
MASFIH had also asked the ministry to arrange meetings with the National Registration Department and the Attorney-General's Chambers so families could receive official explanations from the relevant authorities.
"Family members should not have to keep pursuing meetings just to get answers to questions affecting their status, rights and future," Manivannan said.
A total of 54 Malaysians remain unaccounted for following flash floods in Rasuwagadhi, Nepal, on Aug 26.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High-income districts may still have struggling households
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Living in a district with a high median income does not mean every household is financially comfortable, as lower-income families may still struggle with rising urban living costs.
In a study titled Balancing Fiscal Priorities to Improve Household Wellbeing, Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) researcher Dr Nungsari Ahmad Radhi highlighted the growing financial pressures on lower-income urban households.
The scale of these pressures is also reflected in KRI's State of Households 2026: From Income to Wellbeing report, which found that Malaysia's median household income stood at RM7,017 a month in 2024.
The report found that 46.2 per cent of Malaysian households lived in 22 of the country's 166 districts, where median household income was above the national level.
Not all households in those districts necessarily earned more than RM7,017 a month. Median income is the midpoint of household earnings in a district, meaning half of households earn more and half earn less. A high median income does not mean every household is well-off.
The report also found that 111 districts had poverty rates above the national rate of 5.1 per cent.
Median monthly household expenditure reached RM4,758 in 2024, adding to the financial pressure on families.
Between 2019 and 2024, expenditure among the lower 70 per cent of households by income rose by more than 15 per cent, while spending among the bottom 10 per cent increased by 21.3 per cent.
By 2024, households in the bottom 10 per cent had just 1.8 per cent of their gross income left after consumption expenditure, down from 10.8 per cent in 2019.
The government provides cash and essential-goods assistance to low-income households through Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah, with a combined allocation of RM15 billion in 2026.
The report does not identify which high-income districts have the largest numbers of financially vulnerable households or compare how much income families have left after spending in different districts.
More detailed district-level data on rent, transport, childcare, debt and household income left after spending would help identify families most in need of assistance.
Nungsari said targeted cash assistance based on household needs would be more suitable than determining support based on where people lived.
At the same time, development spending on schools, healthcare facilities, public transport and other public services should be strengthened, particularly in areas undergoing rapid urbanisation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Washington governor calls ICE 'out of control' after airport arrests
Article:
WASHINGTON: The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents "out of control" after they arrested two people at Seattle's main airport on Saturday.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month's midterms.
Video footage widely shared on social media on Saturday showed two people being apprehended by masked men at an airport jet bridge.
ICE later confirmed it had detained two people it said had overstayed their visas.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said the agency was "completely and totally out of control."
"Like many Americans, I'm outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities," Ferguson wrote on X.
"Today's actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE's deeply un-American tactics."
Ferguson said at a news conference that the ICE agents may have broken a state law limiting facial coverings for law enforcement, and that he was looking into how they accessed the jet bridge.
The federal immigration agency said its officers "conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa" on Saturday morning.
The agency confirmed it had detained a second person whom it said would be charged with assaulting a federal officer, alleging she had thrown hot coffee on an ICE agent.
"The individual... was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well," ICE posted on X.
Alaska Airlines, which operated the flight that Mendoza and Mejia tried to board, said on Saturday it was "concerned by this morning's law enforcement action."
"Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials" but does not "direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity", the company added.
The Port of Seattle, which operates the airport, said: "We are outraged about this morning's incident involving ICE and two passengers."
This month, Trump appointed Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff.
Miller faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January – incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russian cargo ship still on fire off Finland after attack
Article:
HELSINKI: A fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to burn through the night even as efforts were made to douse the flames, Finland's coast guard said on Sunday.
The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters where it remains at anchor.
The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship.
Pictures and video released by the coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck.
Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia's northwest coastal Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling onto Nato territory.
The ship, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defence Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.
The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday.
Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.
The Sparta II is a 121-m Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data.
The vessel is subject to US sanctions, according to the US Treasury Department.
Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defence Ministry, according to the company's website.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Red flags put up at four popular beaches in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Red flags have been raised at four beaches in Kelantan due to rough sea conditions during the current Northeast Monsoon.
The beaches are Pantai Geting in Tumpat, Pantai Cahaya Bulan (PCB) in Kota Baru, Pantai Irama in Bachok and Pantai Bisikan Bayu in Pasir Puteh.
Kelantan Civil Defence Force deputy director Mohd Farid Ishak said the red flags had been raised since Oct 27 to warn the public against entering the water due to strong waves and currents.
He said the flags were also placed at coastal areas where waves reached heights of 1.5m to discourage beachgoers from swimming or engaging in other water activities.
"Rough sea conditions pose a serious drowning risk, particularly due to strong underwater currents that could pull swimmers out to sea, even when the water surface appears calm," he said.
Apart from putting up red flags, he said warning signboards had also been installed along the beaches to alert visitors to the dangers.
"Beachgoers are advised not to swim or engage in water activities in areas where red flags have been raised, as the sea conditions are unsafe.
"They should also comply with instructions from the authorities and prioritise their own safety and that of their families," he said.
He said several Civil Defence Force lifeguards had been deployed to monitor the beaches and ensure the public complied with safety directives and stayed out of the water in areas where red flags had been raised.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), the initial phase of the monsoon, from November to January 2027, is expected to bring three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain, which could cause flooding in low-lying areas and locations near rivers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Negri MB Ismail in hospital
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has been hospitalised.
His press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said Ismail was receiving treatment and recovering.
"I have received confirmation regarding Datuk Ismail Lasim's condition," he said in a statement, thanking the public for their concern.
However, the reason for his hospitalisation and the exact time he was admitted remain unclear.
On Friday, it was reported that Ismail would remain as
Negri Sembilan menteri besar
after Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir consented to retain him in the post.
Ismail, 67, who is Juasseh assemblyman, announced told this to reporters at his official residence after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap.
The audience began at 10.30am and ended at 11.35am.
Ismail had said he would remain committed to carrying out the trust and responsibilities entrusted to him.
He also clarified that he had neither submitted nor agreed to the submission of a resignation letter dated Nov 16, as reported earlier.
Earlier, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir had said Tuanku Muhriz had been sent a letter of resignation from Ismail.
The following day, the Negeri Sembilan palace said the resignation would only take effect with Tuanku Muhriz's consent, in accordance with the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Reading habits can keep children from excessive screen time - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parents should encourage their children to read physical books from an early age to build strong literacy skills and reduce their reliance on social media and digital devices.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said without strong reading habits, young people risk spending more time browsing social media platforms such as TikTok rather than exploring quality reading materials that are essential for intellectual development.
"Without a good reading foundation and a sustained interest in reading, our children may end up wanting only to spend time on TikTok or lose interest in exploring storybooks.
"Reading books not only builds vocabulary but also provides us with a much broader experience," he said at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Lembah Pantai MYReaders programme.
Fahmi said while digital technology had become an integral part of daily life, reading physical books should not be sidelined as it remained an important foundation for children's learning and personal development.
He said several developed countries were also placing renewed emphasis on conventional reading and writing practices, including Sweden, where efforts were being made to reduce students' dependence on digital devices.
The Lembah Pantai member of parliament said exposure to reading materials in various languages, including English, should also be strengthened to ensure young people were comfortable communicating in different languages in the future.
To expand the benefits of the literacy initiative, Fahmi said he planned to double the allocation for the MYReaders programme from RM50,000 to RM100,000 next year, in conjunction with its 10th anniversary.
The additional funding would be used to extend classes to several new locations across Lembah Pantai, following feedback from parents who preferred to send their children to classes closer to home.
He also announced RM100 book vouchers for all 54 participants in this year's programme, which was conducted at three locations - the Lembah Pantai Work and Training Centre, the Kerinchi People's Housing Project (PPR) and Sri Cempaka PPR.
The vouchers are intended to encourage participants to purchase new reading materials ahead of the upcoming school holidays.
"Use the vouchers to purchase several books in both Bahasa Melayu and English to help instil a love of reading among children," he said.
Earlier, Fahmi said the programme, now in its ninth year and organised in collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in the constituency, had benefited more than 300 participants.
He said it had helped foster an interest in reading, improve children's spoken English proficiency and build their self-confidence.
Following the encouraging response, Fahmi said he was targeting a 50 to 100 per cent increase in participants next year, depending on the number of tutors and volunteers available.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fluffy rabbits, dark past draw tourists to Japan island
Article:
STEPPING onto an island in western Japan, tourists squeal with joy at the sight of hundreds of fluffy rabbits, but few realise the land was once home to a secret chemical weapons factory for the country's Imperial Army.
Okunoshima – also known as "Rabbit Island" – has a perimeter of just four kilometres but welcomes thousands of snap-happy visitors attracted by its bunny population each year.
"This was my dream," to visit the island, 67-year-old Susan Balzer from Canada told AFP.
"You can feed them, they come to you. We never get to really get close to them" back home, she said.
The rabbit population is thought to have grown from a small group released by a nearby elementary school in the 1970s to around 500 today, aided by abundant food and a lack of predators.
But the island's cute exterior belies a dark history.
In 1929, the former Imperial Japanese Army built a chemical weapons factory on Okunoshima in an effort to catch up with Europe, despite international bans introduced after World War I.
[[nid:1583266]]
As rabbits hop around the island, which lies in the Hiroshima region, large ageing concrete and brick structures – once used as power plants and poison gas depots – serve as reminders of its murky past.
Many of its factory workers suffered from cancer and other diseases, according to a monument on the island.
"Learning that many people died from the gas they produced made me realise what a tragic legacy the island carries," 69-year-old visitor Eiji Tomari said.
"At the same time, I'm glad it has become a place where rabbits can live peacefully."
Since the production of poisonous substances, including mustard gas and lewisite, was highly secretive, authorities removed the island from Japanese maps, keeping it hidden until the end of World War II in 1945, when Allied occupation forces ordered its destruction.
"It was something that could not be disclosed, not just to ordinary citizens, but to the rest of the world," Okunoshima Poison Gas Museum Director Kazuhito Takahashi told AFP.
"If the facility had been exposed internationally, Japan, which relied heavily on imports at the time, could have faced sanctions," he said.
Masayuki Yamauchi, an 82-year-old tour guide, said rabbits were used as test subjects in experiments, although there is no evidence the bunnies now roaming the island descended from them.
"I hope people will learn about that history and use those lessons to help promote peace in the world," Yamauchi said.
[[nid:1583265]]
Last year, around 200,000 people visited the island, according to the local tourism association.
But as word spreads on social media, some experts warn that overfeeding the rabbits is harming the ecosystem.
According to a study published in July, wild boars, lured by the food, have reportedly been observed attacking the creatures.
"To achieve sustainable tourism, it's important to understand the impact of feeding wildlife and to consider how we should interact with it," Asami Ogura, an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology's Kure College, said in a press release on the study.
Ogura said the rabbits face food shortages when there are few tourists, while heavy grazing by the animals has affected the island's vegetation, stripping low-lying branches and leaves from many plants.
Tour guide Yamauchi called the situation "tragic."
"A growing rabbit population does not mean the animals are happy," Yamauchi said.
"If we want them to thrive, visitors should avoid selfishly feeding them."
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amanah wants Gender Parity Act, 30 pct female candidates in polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 Amanah National Convention today passed a motion calling for the enactment of a Gender Parity Act in political representation to ensure that women make up at least 30 per cent of political candidates in the country.
The motion passed with 225 delegates voting aye and 164 nays.
Wanita Amanah chief Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu described the passage of the motion as a significant step forward in efforts to strengthen women's representation in the country's democracy.
She said women's participation in politics could no longer depend solely on discretion, limited opportunities or voluntary commitments, but must instead be strengthened through a clear and effective legal framework supported by an orderly implementation mechanism.
"The minimum 30 per cent target for female candidates is not a privilege, but an affirmative measure to ensure women have a fair opportunity to contribute, lead and shape the country's future.
"I would like to thank all delegates who tabled and supported this motion.
"May its approval serve as a starting point for more concrete action, rather than remaining merely a resolution on paper," she said in a Facebook post.
Aiman Athirah said the motion's approval also represented a political mandate from Amanah for the government to move from commitment to action, aspirations to legislation, and participation to meaningful representation.
"Amanah believes that democracy will never be truly complete as long as half of the country's leadership potential is not given the opportunity it deserves," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: 'Big tent' proposal must first be discussed by PH presidential council
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The "big tent" proposal and other political strategies involving Pakatan Harapan should first be brought to its presidential council for discussion and not aired publicly, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
"Everyone has their own views and suggestions, but I believe that if we make suggestions publicly and discuss them through the media, we will not achieve the desired intentions or objectives," he told reporters after opening the Selangor DAP 2026 Convention here today.
He was commenting on Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil's suggestion that PH adopt a "big tent" approach and embrace more Malay-based parties to boost support among Malay voters ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Loke also said DAP was open to the proposal for component parties to use their respective party logos in GE16, but this would require further discussions within PH before a final decision was made.
"What is most important is that we must consolidate our strength and find the best approach to face the election. However, such a proposal must first be discussed at the presidential council.
"DAP will give its views, and of course, we have suggestions on how to move forward in the coming election," he said.
On another matter, Loke said the status of his resignation as transport minister on Nov 10 was subject to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's decision.
"As far as I'm concerned, I already resigned," he said.
Anwar had previous said the government need not rush into deciding on
Loke's resignation
, although the official letter on the matter had been received, adding that it required careful consideration.
The previous day, Loke had reiterated his decision to stand by his resignation with immediate effect following the High Court's decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Landslide shuts down two lanes, but Cameron Highlands route remains accessible
Article:
GUA MUSANG: The route to Cameron Highlands remains accessible to motorists, although two of the four lanes along FT185 Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang have been closed following a landslide yesterday.
Kelantan Public Works Department (PWD) director Nik Badlihisham Nik Ismail said motorists could still proceed via a diversion route provided at the affected stretch.
He said the closure involved only the two left lanes of the dual carriageway.
"PWD will apply for an allocation to carry out repair works at the affected area in the near future.
"Motorists are advised to always comply with the warning signs installed, particularly when passing through the diversion route," he told reporters.
Yesterday, the left lane at Section 84.15 of federal route FT185 Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang, near Yayasan Albarakah, heading towards Cameron Highlands, had been closed to all vehicles following a
landslide
.
The incident affected an area measuring 20m in length and 30m in depth, while an inspection also detected cracks along a 30m stretch of the road.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sanusi's daughter discharged from hospital 9 days after motorcycle crash
Article:
KULIM: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's daughter, who was injured in a motorcycle crash on Nov 12, was discharged from hospital yesterday.
The Kedah menteri besar said his third child was previously treated at the intensive care unit of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) in Alor Star for four days before being transferred to a regular ward.
He said his daughter now needs to wear braces on her spine and arm, in addition to undergoing follow-up dental treatment for injuries to her mouth.
"A nurse will come (to the house) three times a week to clean and dress her wounds," he told reporters after opening the state level 2026 World Town Planning Day celebration in Taman Tasik Putra.
It was
reported
that Sanusi's daughter suffered injuries to her head and face and broke four fingers and ribs after the motorcycle she was riding crashed.
The 20-year-old had been riding from her college in Pokok Sena towards Alor Star about 4pm when the incident occurred.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pushers target pupils with 'piu-piu' vapes via social media, delivery services
Article:
SEREMBAN: Drug trafficking syndicates are increasingly using social media and closed-group applications to market electronic cigarettes (vapes) containing synthetic drugs, locally known as 'piu-piu', with the products delivered to buyers, including students, through courier and delivery services.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the modus operandi allowed transactions to take place without direct contact between sellers and buyers, making it more difficult for the police to detect such activities.
"Communication between sellers and buyers takes place through specific platforms, including dark web sites, which act as intermediaries and allow them to connect discreetly to obtain the illicit substances.
"Payments are made online, after which the products are delivered to buyers through e-hailing or courier services. Based on our intelligence, a single cartridge is sold for between RM50 and RM100, depending on its quality and contents," he told Bernama.
He said the misuse of vapes containing drug-laced liquids, or 'piu-piu', was first detected in Negri Sembilan last year and has since emerged as a growing concern, particularly among students.
Alzafny said police had identified three cases involving secondary school students in the state over the past three years, comprising one case in May and two others early this month.
Tests on the seized vape liquids found that they contained various drugs, including methamphetamine, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) and ketamine, he added.
It was reported that a 17-year-old male
student
in Nilai had tested positive for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).
The student is being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him in an intoxicated state, allegedly after using a vape.
Meanwhile, Alzafny said family-related problems and emotional stress were among the factors that could lead individuals to misuse drug-laced vapes, with some turning to the substances in an attempt to relieve stress.
"They may also use these vapes in search of new experiences because they produce an intoxicating effect, unlike ordinary vapes," he said.
He said teenagers were also attracted to the devices' modern designs, appealing scents and portability, which made them easy to conceal.
Alzafny said all district police chiefs had been instructed to intensify surprise inspections at schools, particularly in hostel areas.
Police would also introduce a 'Heart to Heart' programme featuring open discussions between officers and students to raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse.
He urged local authorities to review permits issued for vape sales, particularly to ensure that students could not easily access the products, and advised parents to take a more active role in monitoring their children's social circles.
"Parents should also regularly check their children's personal belongings, such as school bags, to determine whether they possess vape devices or are involved in drug abuse.
"Early warning signs include behavioural changes, such as a loss of self-control or actions that are out of character," he said.
Commenting on the supply of drug-laced vape products in the state, Alzafny said police had recently arrested two foreign nationals and seized 732 cartridges containing a total of 7,320 millilitres of a substance suspected to be ketamine, worth RM219,600, at a residence in the Klang Valley last October.
He said those involved in supplying or distributing vape liquids containing drugs could face action under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, while students found to be involved would be referred to the National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) for treatment and rehabilitation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DID forecasts flooding in Kelantan districts from Nov 24
Article:
KOTA BARU: Flooding could hit Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah and Tumpat in Kelantan from Nov 24 to 27, according to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
In its preliminary flood forecast for Kelantan today, the department said its analysis of hydrological data using a flood forecasting model identified flood hotspots, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations in the four districts as particularly at risk.
The department said flooding could occur earlier or later than forecast and advised disaster management agencies and residents, particularly those in areas likely to be affected, to stay alert and follow instructions from the authorities.
DID said it would continue monitoring the river basins concerned and issue flood warnings if heavy rain persisted.
In Jeli, the areas at risk are in the Sungai Golok basin and include Sungai Buloh, Sungai Lanas, Sungai Legeh and Sungai Satan.
In Pasir Mas, the areas at risk include Sungai Golok, Sungai Bunut Susu, Sungai Meranti, Sungai Tandak, Sungai Kedotok, Sungai Lanchang, Tasik Garu, Tasik Danau To' Uban, Sungai Rengas, Sungai Lemal and Sungai Lemal Mati.
The forecast for Tanah Merah covers Sungai Golok, Sungai Jegor, Sungai Manal, Sungai Jedok, Sungai Air Bujing and Sungai Lanas.
In Tumpat, the department identified Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua, Sungai Gali, Sungai Kelaboran and Sungai Tapang as areas at risk.
The public can check the latest flood information and warnings at publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my or on the PublicInfoBanjir Facebook page.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SMS alerts to remain for phones that don't support disaster warning system - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Smartphone users whose devices do not meet the minimum specifications for the disaster early warning system will not be left out of emergency alerts, as notifications via short message service (SMS) will continue to be available.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the existing notification mechanism operated by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) would continue as usual to ensure all segments of society received timely warnings.
"So, the SMS notification system is still in place, and Nadma can certainly implement it. It is already available now," he told a press conference after attending the closing ceremony of the MYReaders Lembah Pantai 2026 programme.
He said the Early Warning System (EWS) developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would not replace existing mechanisms but would complement them to strengthen the dissemination of disaster information to the public.
Fahmi said in areas prone to flooding, particularly along river corridors, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) had installed warning sirens as part of its preparedness measures.
On Nov 19, MCMC urged
smartphone
users to update their devices to support EWS alerts, with the minimum requirements being an iPhone 11 or newer running iOS 27.2 or later, Android phones running Android 12 or later, and Huawei devices running EMUI 16 or later.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said an initial EWS test would be conducted specifically at Parliament tomorrow about 1.30pm.
The exercise would allow MPs to see how alert notifications appeared on their mobile phones before informing their constituents and explaining how the system worked.
He said a full-scale test of the system was scheduled to be conducted simultaneously nationwide on Nov 29, with the time to be confirmed soon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No shortcuts, no instant paste: How Banglo289 keeps traditional Malay cuisine authentic at mid-market prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 —  In an increasingly competitive food and beverage industry, the use of instant ingredients and commercial pastes has become a common choice among food operators, particularly to save preparation time and reduce costs.
However, Banglo289, a restaurant serving traditional Malay cuisine from various states, has chosen to go against the grain by using fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods to preserve the authenticity of its dishes.
The restaurant also offers a unique dining concept, combining an upscale and comfortable setting with prices aimed at the mid-market segment.
“The idea behind setting up this restaurant actually stemmed from our observation of a gap in the market for traditional food, particularly Malay cuisine, served in a comfortable setting at reasonable prices.
“Usually, if customers want to enjoy this type of food at affordable prices, roadside stalls are their best option, but the surroundings may not be very comfortable. If they prefer a more comfortable setting, there are exclusive restaurants, but they have to pay premium prices,” its Chief Executive Officer Shareen Farzida Sukri told Bernama.
Making heritage cuisine accessible
Banglo289 seeks to bridge that gap by offering an exclusive dining environment and a wide selection of dishes, allowing customers to choose their preferred food and portions according to their tastes and budgets.
The Kelantan-born entrepreneur from Kuala Krai said the average spending of between RM30 and RM50 per person per visit recorded by the restaurant did not refer to the fixed price of any particular dish, but rather the total amount customers typically spent during each visit.
“This includes a combination of rice, side dishes, vegetables, porridge, desserts, fruits and traditional cakes, all reflected in a single bill,” she explained.
The menu also varies according to dining hours, with different selections available for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Recounting the restaurant’s establishment in 2022, Shareen Farzida said that, as its name suggests, the premises occupy a century-old bungalow located along Jalan Raja Chulan here.
Within four years of operation, the restaurant brand has expanded to four outlets at different locations across the Klang Valley, with plans to open more branches in other states nationwide.
Balancing costs and business sustainability
The expansion has also brought greater responsibilities, particularly in ensuring that the concept and quality of food remain consistent across all outlets, a task Shareen Farzida acknowledged posed challenges, especially in terms of costs.
Using fresh ingredients, including spices, requires employees to prepare basic ingredients themselves, such as fresh chillies, onions and turmeric.
“The cost of fresh coconut milk alone reaches RM50,000 a month for all our outlets. We adopt this approach to ensure the authenticity of our food.
“Previous generations, such as our mothers and grandmothers, rarely or never used instant ingredients, possibly because of preservatives and chemicals that could affect the original taste of the dishes,” she said.
To demonstrate its commitment to preparing basic ingredients from scratch without relying on instant pastes, the restaurant has incorporated open-kitchen concepts near the serving counters at almost all its outlets, allowing customers to observe the cooking process firsthand.
Minimising food wastage
Shareen Farzida said rising raw material prices were managed through careful operational planning to ensure that the restaurant did not compromise on food quality.
“Among the cost-saving measures we have introduced are those that do not affect the taste of our food, such as opting for simpler decorations and food presentation that are not overly elaborate but remain neat and visually appealing.
“We also focus on improving workforce management by arranging staff shifts and allocating duties according to peak and off-peak hours, ensuring productivity remains high without placing an excessive burden on salary costs,” she explained.
The restaurant also prioritises efficient raw material management, with each outlet having its own purchasing team to source fresh ingredients according to the respective kitchen’s requirements.
“Raw ingredients must be used on the same day and cannot be kept for use on another day.
“We have adopted this approach to minimise wastage and keep our overhead costs under control. This is why dishes are prepared in stages and in small batches of only about 10 to 15 servings at a time, with no leftover dishes kept for the following day.
“If a particular dish is in high demand, additional portions can be prepared as long as operating hours and the availability of raw ingredients permit,” she said.
She added that the restaurant sometimes had to explain its concept to customers, particularly its practice of preparing food in controlled quantities to maintain quality and prevent wastage.
Nevertheless, she said certain best-selling dishes, such as smoked beef cooked in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies (daging salai masak lemak cili api), were always made available to customers.
Traditional cooking
To preserve the authenticity of its traditional dishes, Banglo289 also takes the initiative to learn heritage cooking techniques directly from their original sources.
Banglo289 Business Development Director Datuk Mohd Hafidz Safari Ramli said research teams, usually comprising between six and 12 chefs, travelled to selected states, including Kelantan, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Johor, to meet veteran cooks and local communities who still possessed knowledge of traditional food preparation.
“This research is an ongoing learning process. Each visit is not merely about obtaining a list of ingredients, but also understanding the entire process, from selecting raw materials and determining measurements to the sequence of cooking steps and the time required to produce an authentic dish,” he said.
He added that the teams would revisit the original sources if their attempts to recreate a dish did not meet the desired characteristics, whether in terms of taste, colour or texture.
Every recipe and cooking method learnt is documented as a reference for the chefs, helping to ensure consistent food quality even when dishes are prepared by different individuals.
Citing Kelantan’s nasi dagang as an example, he said the team not only learnt its preparation methods directly from local sources in the state but also sourced ingredients, including spices, from there.
For patin fish cooked in fermented durian paste gravy (patin masak tempoyak), the research team travelled to Temerloh, Pahang, to understand the balance of sourness and the distinctive consistency of the gravy.
Meanwhile, the preparation of smoked beef in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies involves manually smoking the meat over rambutan wood and coconut shells for approximately eight hours.
“All these are part of the preparation process that cannot simply be bypassed. If we want to preserve our cultural heritage through food, we must do it properly and uphold the true meaning of the word ‘heritage’,” he said.
Reviving endangered heritage dishes
Apart from preserving the authenticity of traditional dishes that remain familiar to the public, Banglo289 is also committed to reviving heritage cuisine that is becoming increasingly difficult to find, particularly dishes that are no longer widely prepared by restaurant operators or younger generations.
Shareen Farzida said the initiative, known as ‘Endangered Recipes’, stemmed from her team’s observations of the diversity of traditional food in several locations, including dishes that were known or still prepared by only a handful of food operators and elderly cooks.
Among the dishes identified for preservation are lemang periuk kera, kulat sisir masak lemak, lawar terung and bubur anak lebah, each with its own distinctive ingredients and preparation techniques.
Citing bubur anak lebah as an example, she explained that the traditional sweet delicacy, made from a rice flour-based batter, requires considerable manual skill and a special mould to shape tiny pieces resembling baby bees before they are cooked until chewy and served with sweet coconut milk gravy.
Preparing such unique dishes requires patience and direct guidance, as the techniques cannot necessarily be mastered through written recipes alone, she said.
She added that the team’s visits to several states had also uncovered dishes that were prepared only during Ramadan or certain festive seasons, limiting opportunities for younger generations to discover and learn how to make them.
This has raised concerns that the knowledge and skills involved could disappear if those who still possess them pass away before having the opportunity to pass them on.
“That is why we plan to collaborate with Yayasan Hasanah, an impact-driven foundation under Khazanah Nasional Berhad that actively supports the preservation of local arts, heritage and culture, to fund the production of a special documentary on this ongoing project.
“Heritage cuisine is not merely a cultural treasure to be printed on a menu. It is a body of knowledge and a cultural identity that must continue to be cooked, savoured, documented and passed down properly, without shortcuts,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Thailand only a transit route for drug syndicates targeting Malaysia, says Kelantan police chief after 700kg meth bust
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 21 — Malaysia-Thailand cross-border security cooperation has continued to strengthen, with authorities in the neighbouring country successfully preventing more than 700 kilogrammes of methamphetamine from entering Malaysia.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the success demonstrated the Thai authorities’ commitment to combating drug smuggling activities that use the country as a transit route before the drugs are brought into Malaysia.
He said Thailand was not the main destination for the drug smuggling activities but served primarily as a transit route for syndicates involved in cross-border crime.
Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police had previously held meetings with the Thai authorities to strengthen security cooperation, particularly in combating drug smuggling and criminal activities along the border of the two countries.
“The Thai authorities have taken steps to tighten security by setting up checkpoints to prevent cross-border criminal activities, including the entry of drugs into Malaysia.
“What we have implemented on our side has also been adopted by Thailand, and they have now stepped up their security measures. We are grateful for the cooperation and commitment shown,” he told reporters after an engagement programme with young bikers at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here today.
Mohd Yusoff said close cooperation between the two countries was important to ensure that border routes were not exploited by syndicates to carry out drug smuggling activities.
He said enhanced joint security measures could also help curb the movement of syndicates using cross-border routes to smuggle illicit substances into the country. — Bernama

Title: Four teenagers under 15 arrested after ramming police car during chase on North-South Expressway
Article:
IPOH, Nov 21 — Police detained four underage teenagers (under 15 years old) for allegedly obstructing public servants from performing their duties at Kilometre 286.5 of the North-South Expressway heading north, near Simpang Pulai, yesterday.
Tapah district deputy police chief DSP Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of officers on patrol duty received information at 4.20 pm yesterday from the Tapah district police headquarters (IPD) control centre to assist officers from the Ringlet police station in tracking down a Toyota Cherry multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several individuals suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case.
He said that following the information, police officers moved to the Batu 3 area, Jalan Pahang, near Tapah, to conduct a surveillance and the vehicle involved was successfully detected at about 5.30 pm.
“The police instructed the driver of the vehicle to stop for inspection, but the driver failed to comply with the order and instead sped off, nearly hitting the on-duty police officer.
“The police officers then gave chase to the vehicle all the way to the Tapah toll plaza area. In an effort to intercept the suspect’s vehicle, the police vehicle’s bumper was hit by the suspect’s vehicle,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Fadzil said another police vehicle from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined in the chase before the suspect’s vehicle was successfully intercepted at Simpang Pulai.
He said all four suspects were arrested, and the vehicle they used was seized.
According to him, the initial investigation found that all those detained were teenagers and the results of the urine screening tests showed that they were all drug-free and had no previous records.
“The three teenage boys who were detained have been remanded for four days starting today, while a teenage girl was granted police bail as she is involved in an ongoing investigation in Jitra, Kedah,” he also said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code as well as Section 279 and Section 353 of the same code. — Bernama

Title: Don’t push your child into a boarding school if they’re not ready, Fadhlina tells parents as Education Ministry weighs more wardens and counsellors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Ministry of Education is looking into the need to increase the number of assistant wardens and guidance and counselling teachers to ensure students receive optimal attention and support while staying in hostels.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children’s own abilities and emotional readiness.
“As we plan for our children’s future, it is important that we also listen to their voices and understand their feelings. Our dreams as parents must align with our children’s own abilities and emotional readiness,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, she said that she had held discussions with the police in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, on strengthening the safety and well-being of students residing in the hostel of the educational institution concerned.
The discussions covered compliance with standard operating procedures, hostel management, and the importance of parents assessing their children’s level of readiness before sending them to boarding schools.
Fadhlina said every child had a different level of adaptability, with some adjusting quickly while others required more time, adding that some children were able to cope well with academic competition, while others needed greater encouragement.
As such, she stressed the importance of creating an environment where children could share their thoughts and be heard without being judged.
“I want parents to know that we share the same hopes. We want our children to succeed, but more importantly, we want them to grow up safe and happy,” she added.
She also advised parents not to be overly concerned if their children do not gain admission to their dream schools, as every child has his or her own unique path and timeline for achieving success.
“Most importantly, regardless of where they study, they must know that our love and acceptance never depend on the name of their school or their examination results,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Bumiputera firms are listing on Bursa, but Akmal Nasrullah wants them to go bigger
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Five Bumiputera companies successfully listed on Bursa Malaysia between April 2025 and September 2026, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
The companies are Orkim Bhd, which was listed on the Main Market, and SumiSaujana Group Bhd, Elsa Bhd, GTA Holdings Bhd and United Asiapac Energy Bhd, which were listed on the ACE Market.
Akmal Nasrullah said the listings demonstrated the potential of Bumiputera enterprises to grow, attract investment and gain access to broader capital markets.
“Our next challenge is to build on this progress by enabling more Bumiputera enterprises to scale up, compete in higher-value industries and become market leaders,” he said in his opening remarks at the YP Leadership Conference 2026 here today.
He highlighted that under the 13th Malaysia Plan, Malaysia aims to raise its economic potential while raising the floor of living standards.
“The Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 complements this direction by advancing meaningful Bumiputera participation, ownership and competitiveness.
“Human capital development is fundamental to both agendas, but it must be closely linked to enterprise growth and economic opportunities,” he said.
“This is where the complementary roles of Yayasan Peneraju, the Bumiputera Agenda Steering Unit (Teraju) and Ekuiti Nasional Bhd (Ekuinas) become especially important.
“Together, their mandates support an ecosystem that develops talent, strengthens enterprises, facilitates business expansion and promotes long-term economic ownership,” he added.
He said Yayasan Peneraju identifies and nurtures high-potential talents to become value creators in professional, business and community spheres.
Meanwhile, Teraju supports the development and expansion of Bumiputera enterprises, while Ekuinas contributes through investment, business transformation and long-term value creation. — Bernama

Title: Pahang puts RM450,000 into hunt for invasive redtail catfish threatening native fish
Article:
TEMERLOH, Nov 21 — The Pahang government has allocated RM450,000 for a programme to control the redtail catfish population, which has been identified as a potential threat to the state’s native fish population if left unchecked.
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the programme, being carried out simultaneously at seven locations statewide, including Pekan and Jerantut as well as Temerloh, was aimed at reducing the population of the invasive fish species.
He said the redtail catfish was a predatory alien species that could threaten the survival of other native fish species sharing the same habitat.
“The state government takes the issue of redtail catfish very seriously as this is an alien species that can threaten existing fish populations.
“If left unchecked, it could wipe out native species because it is highly aggressive and preys on other fish, eventually becoming the dominant species,” he said.
